n8n.note: A second, real local n8n instance stood up for this capture (Docker Desktop, named container + named persistent volume, both reversible). Imported via `n8n import:workflow`, activated via `n8n publish:workflow`, exercised while the real Lead Rescue app ran via `npm run dev` on localhost:3000, reachable from the container as host.docker.internal:3000.

n8nExecution.source: n8n execution_entity row id=4, read directly from the local n8n instance's own SQLite database (database.sqlite, execution_entity + execution_data tables) after the run — not inferred from the HTTP response.

httpRequest.note: The external trigger payload (POSTed to n8n's real webhook at http://localhost:5678/webhook/lead-rescue-ingress) was mapped into this canonical envelope by n8n's own 'Validate / Envelope' node — the sourceEventId and source values above are n8n's real, recorded output for that node, read from execution_data, not authored into this file directly.

durableApplicationState.source: read directly from .data/lead-rescue-wait-incidents.json (the real FileWaitIncidentStore-backed persistence layer) after the execution, not copied from the HTTP response body.

n8nExecution.source: n8n execution_entity row id=3, read directly from the local n8n instance's own SQLite database after the run. mode='trigger' (not 'manual' or 'webhook') is n8n's own record that its Schedule Trigger fired this execution on its own clock — no curl, click, or CLI invocation from this pass caused it.
n8nExecution.additionalExecutionsNote: Three genuine schedule-fired executions (ids 1, 2, 3) were recorded in the ~3 minutes the activated workflow ran unattended before this capture, one per minute, matching the workflow's configured 1-minute interval. Only id=3 is detailed above as the representative sample; ids 1-2 are structurally identical (same target route, same 200/empty-results outcome, since no incident was yet past a timeout deadline).

httpRequest.note: The wait-sweep workflow deliberately sends no body and no incidentId — see the workflow's own sticky note. It asks only 'has anything become due', never a specific business question, so there is no per-request sourceEventId for this workflow by design.

durableApplicationState.note: No waiting incident was past its configured timeout deadline at the moment this real, n8n-triggered sweep ran, so checkAllWaitingIncidents genuinely found nothing to act on — an honest negative result, not a fabricated one. The sweep's real HTTP round trip into the app and its real, empty 'results' array are the durable proof; no record needed to change for the sweep itself to be genuinely exercised through n8n.

providerMode.note: LEAD_RESCUE_DECISION_PROVIDER was not set to 'claude' for this capture, so app/api/lead-rescue/ingress/route.ts's resolveIngressDecisionProvider() selected FixtureDecisionProvider — confirmed above by httpResponse.classifierProvider === 'fixture-decision-provider' on the real ingress response, not merely asserted here.

sideEffectMode.note: executionMode: 'SIMULATED' on the real ingress response confirms no real third-party side effect was attempted for this case. No offer-dispatch or notification side effect fired during this capture window (the created case reached BOOKING_READY only); every existing SideEffectExecutor in this codebase (AlwaysSucceedsSimulatedExecutor and its test variants) remains simulated regardless.

scopeStatement: This evidence proves that a real local n8n runtime (v2.35.7, Docker) genuinely executed both committed Lead Rescue workflows (n8n/workflows/lead-rescue-ingress.json via a real webhook delivery, n8n/workflows/lead-rescue-wait-sweep.json via its own Schedule Trigger firing unattended) and crossed the real Lead Rescue application HTTP boundary, producing durable application state through the real file-backed persistence layer. It does NOT prove real Anthropic classification — the decision provider was fixture-backed for this capture, never the live ClaudeDecisionProvider. It does NOT prove real outbound third-party message delivery — no email, SMS, or CRM provider was contacted; every side effect this capture touched remains simulated, and no production credential, endpoint, or deployment exists anywhere in this path.
